comparable_reason: The landscape statistics are width-invariant but magnitude-dominated. Under a zero-padding isometry of a 40x64 cloud into d = 256 and 1024 the values are BIT-IDENTICAL (max_1 = 5.425195217, integral_1 = 29.432743144, norm_1 = 10.317570041), so ambient dimension is not the problem. github_repo: scikit-tda/persim (PersLandscapeExact) plus Bubenik & Dlotko's Persistence Landscape Toolbox
github_reason: Bubenik released the Persistence Landscape Toolbox with the follow-up paper; for this round I cross-checked against persim 0.3.8's `PersLandscapeExact` (the maintained Python implementation of Bubenik's Def. 3) and against an independent exact reference I wrote from the definition -- the complete breakpoint set (all births, deaths, apexes and all pairwise crossings (b_i+d_j)/2), with the exact per-segment closed forms (b-a)(y_a+y_b)/2 for the integral and (b-a)(y_a^2+y_a y_b+y_b^2)/3 for the squared L2. BLME matches persim's maxima to 5.08e-16 over six diagrams and my reference to 0.0 (maxima), 0.0 (integrals) and 2.61e-16 (norms) over 12 diagrams of 2-199 bars, plus 0.0/0.0/1.48e-16 on a 2,999-bar diagram. Above the cap the reference is what establishes that the maxima remain exact (3.010000000 on all five levels) while the integrals are the +2.4618% / -3.8285% now labelled refined_approximation.
paper_reason: Bubenik (JMLR 16:77-102, 2015) Prop. 5 gives the whole-landscape L1 norm in closed form as sum_i (d_i - b_i)^2 / 4 and the L-infinity norm as max_i (d_i - b_i)/2. For the two-bar diagram {[0,12], [4,16]} the published forms give 72 and 6; BLME returns per-level integrals [56.0, 16.0, 0.0, 0.0, 0.0] summing to 72.0 and landscape_max_1 = 6.0, relative error 0.00e+00 on both.
confounds_reason: Not an architectural confound: the statistics are bit-identical under a zero-padding isometry from d = 64 to 1024, and the 54-model archive gives layer_0_h0_landscape_max_1 rho(d_model) = -0.082, rho(n_layers) = +0.017, rho(params) = -0.065 (all null; the largest is rho(vocab) = -0.252). SUSPECTED rather than NONE because the metric IS a pure power of the representation scale (exactly degree 1 / 3/2 / 2, measured to 9 digits), so any systematic difference in activation magnitude between model families propagates straight into the reported number -- and the archive's 170-fold spread in layer_0_h0_landscape_max_1 is far larger than any topological difference these clouds can carry.
